transcript.answer:
Collection: every Lore service (lore-api, the stations service, and the lore-mcp gateway) serves OpenTelemetry metrics as Prometheus text on a dedicated `metrics` port. The default is 9464, set by `LORE_METRICS_PORT`, and the exporter is `@opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus`. lore-api hands the Prometheus reader to its NodeSDK, and traces still go to Cloud Trace. The stations service and the gateway have no NodeSDK, so each registers its own MeterProvider through `startPrometheusMetrics`. The Helm charts expose the `metrics` port on the Services, and a ServiceMonitor scrapes it. The Cloud Monitoring metric exporter was removed. A terraform-installed kube-prometheus-stack does the scraping. It also scrapes the floor's and the agent controller's own `/metrics`.

Instruments are defined in `libs/shared/src/outbound/otel/metrics.ts` and resolved lazily against the global meter provider. Examples: `lore.http.requests`, `lore.http.duration_ms`, `lore.station.runs`, `lore.station.duration_ms`, `lore.bus.deliveries`, `lore.bus.queue_depth`, `lore.llm.*` (calls, tokens, cost), and `lore.billed.cost_usd`.

Viewing: Grafana in the same stack shows them on dashboards. Grafana sits behind an oauth2-proxy using the Headlamp-style Google login. The dashboards listed in the memory are factory overview, assembly line, agent controller, services and spend. Grafana also reads GKE pod metrics through a Cloud Monitoring datasource. Separately, the web UI analytics page at `/analytics` shows task, latency and token-usage data, and the `lore_get_analytics` MCP tool returns the same data.

ADR-050 has status 'in progress'. The memory notes that the stack was built but not yet applied.

judgements.reason: The answer covers every essential point in the gold: OpenTelemetry Prometheus text on port 9464, scraping by a terraform-installed kube-prometheus-stack, Grafana for viewing, and Cloud Trace for traces via lore-api's NodeSDK only, and nothing it adds contradicts the gold.
